goal: Judge a repository's first public impression and route non-user items
prompt: Look at {{FIXTURES}}/user/presentation. It is a Pi extension I am about to publish. repo-meta.json stands in for its GitHub About box and settings. Tell me how it will look to someone who lands on the GitHub or npm page for the first time, and what to fix first. Do not edit the files.
expected_behavior: Leads with the visitor's view: no About text, topics or homepage, and a one-word package description (repo-meta.json, package.json)
Ranks the README first screen as MUST: caveats and a compatibility matrix before any pitch, install buried at the end, internals in the README
Finds the missing 'what leaves your machine' disclosure and the unflagged permission bypass (src/tidy.ts sends the file and 20 turns, runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions, writes in place)
Flags the demo GIF's relative URL (will not render on the npm page) and that the usage block's inline annotations break copied commands
Flags engines >=18 against CI testing only Node 22, and notes-scratch.md shipping in package files, as present/missing items in a 'For B' section without reconfiguring CI
Gives MUST/SHOULD/NICE ranks with evidence and exact proposed text, and states what it could not view (the live GitHub and npm pages)
hard_failures: Edits fixture files or CI configuration
Claims to have checked a live GitHub or npm page
Invents features, users or metrics not in the fixture
Judges CI or repository settings in depth instead of routing them to B

scoring.scale: 0 = absent/incorrect; 1 = partial or needs material steering; 2 = correct with evidence
scoring.pass: Every criterion at least 1, average at least 1.75, no hard failure; retain evidence and intervention count
